result.title: Predicting Rare-Mode Collapse in Recursive Generative Training from Single-Generation Calibration
result.summary: Recursive generative training can preserve sample counts in a rare region while silently eroding its characteristic core. Mapping this finite-horizon collapse across real-data quotas, rare prevalences, and feedback perturbations via exhaustive multi-generation chains is computationally prohibitive. We develop a decoupled framework that forecasts multi-generation collapse probabilities and locates operating risk boundaries from independent single-generation conditional fits alone. Pairing an exact three-source multinomial count law with single-generation response banks propagates count marginals in closed form, backed by explicit calibration-error and boundary-resolution bounds. For additive Gaussian perturbations, we further prove that equal-variance all-row and sparse policies reverse their boundary-crossing order at a unique hyperplane distance. Across a 2,178-setting count benchmark, exact propagation cuts risk mean absolute error (MAE) from 1.85 to 0.49 percentage points (pp). Across ten two-dimensional learners, calibration achieves 2.60--5.69~pp six-round core MAE on nine stationary learners (65--81\% below an unperturbed baseline), diagnoses non-stationary outlier drift in standard DDIM (16.38~pp) via a stability probe, and resolves the predicted six-round geometric reversal. On Fashion-MNIST latent flow-matching chains, calibration outperforms direct-chain Gaussian-process interpolation at lower fit budgets and tracks the 20\% latent-perturbation boundary shift (3.14 versus 10.78~pp MAE for proportion copying) driven by opposing inflow to the rare region and outflow from its core.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出解耦框架，利用单代条件拟合与精确计数传播，预测递归生成训练中稀有模式在多代后的坍缩概率和风险边界，并在计数基准、二维学习器及 Fashion-MNIST latent flow-matching 链上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 「用单步校准预测多步递归退化」及稀有核心坍缩，可能类比 latent 推理中的信息坍缩与长度泛化预测，但研究对象是生成训练而非 VLM 推理，联系较远，可供核查。
